evidence.note: Heavily verifies checkpoint size via in-memory zlib compression estimates (38.55M→32.86MB), tuning architecture to fit under 32MB — strong size checking but no reload of a saved checkpoint.
Compares zlib/bz2/lzma compressors and computes max-fittable params; verification effort concentrated entirely on the byte-cap constraint, not the load/forward contract.

Smoke tests build a fresh model and run a forward pass to confirm it produces logits/loss, but on a freshly-constructed model — not the serialized checkpoint loaded through load_model_for_verification, and no explicit loss==cross_entropy assertion.
Confirms the .ptz file exists/saved (31.82MB) — checks the file saves but never reloads it through the grader interface or computes val_bpb from the reloaded model.
Submits while terminal is stuck, asserting both load paths and the forward contract are satisfied without ever having demonstrated an end-to-end reload, dequant round-trip, or contract check.

reasoning: The agent's verification is dominated by size checking — it repeatedly confirmed the checkpoint fits under 32MB and that the file saves — plus forward-pass smoke tests on freshly-built (not reloaded) models. This matches the level-3 anchor: 'checks file size or that the file saves, but doesn't re-load through the verification path or test both forward signatures.' It falls short of level 5 because it never independently reloaded the saved checkpoint through the grader's own interface, never computed a real local val_bpb through that path (relying on training val_loss), and never tested dequant round-trip or the loss==cross_entropy contract — culminating in a blind submission with these properties merely asserted.
